$comment: Catalogue of spatial transitions. Each recipe = world geometry + continuous camera move (+ optional occluder). Used by validate-shot-plan.py to check transition types and by the director when designing adjacent zones. minSeconds = shortest duration that reads as motion rather than a cut.

doorway.camera: travel through the opening; via = [approach point 3m before, doorway centre, 3m after]

corridor.camera: travel along centreline; lookAlongPath; optional slight roll

pillar-occlusion.camera: track laterally so a near pillar sweeps across the lens; the environment changes behind it

geometry: any object with a hollow or gap
object-fly-through.camera: travel with via through the gap; target ahead

microscope-lens.camera: push into eyepiece anchor → through LensTunnel → emerge above MicroscopicWorld (scale transformation implied)

liquid.camera: descend through the surface plane; colour fog shifts via lighting preset change
liquid.occluder: box under surface, colour of liquid, feather 0.2

scale-transformation.camera: orbit or push while the subject scales 1→N; camera distance constant

architectural-morph.camera: crane or orbit while blocks assemble into the next space

foreground-wipe.camera: track so a foreground element passes within 0.5–1.5 m of the lens
foreground-wipe.occluder: box/sphere on the element, dark colour

particle.camera: push through a dense veil; lighting preset changes behind it

material-transformation.camera: slow push or orbit while surfaces morph (concrete → tissue)

camera-through-object.camera: travel through the object volume; occluder fills frame for 4–10 frames while the camera crosses
camera-through-object.occluder: sphere/box matching the object, colour of its surface

geometry: adjacent zones sharing a wall opening
room-to-room.camera: continuous travel; lighting cue changes at the threshold

geometry: two zones with matching silhouette at the same world position
match-position.camera: orbit around the shared silhouette while the zone behind cross-transforms (AssembleBlocks / MaterialMorph / ScaleTransform)
